chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Isma'il ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the prayer over the deceased. He said: As for the believer, then it is five takbirs; and as for the hypocrite, then it is four; and there is no salam in it.

key_terms.الْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person over whom the prayer is performed
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: the believer, for whom five takbirs are prescribed
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُ: the hypocrite, for whom four takbirs are prescribed
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَاتٍ: the pronouncements of 'Allahu Akbar' in the funeral prayer
key_terms.سَلَامَ: the concluding salutation, which is negated here

ai.seo_question: How many takbirs are said in the funeral prayer, and is there a salam in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat over the deceased. It distinguishes between the believer and the hypocrite in the number of takbirs, and states that there is no salam in this prayer.
